decisions.reason: ACE3 was publicly launched as the firm's new industry-standard ALCMS control platform and sits at the core of its airfield lighting business, so the heavy investment and visible commitment make continuation very likely.

The air situation display supports the firm's announced push into integrated surveillance and airport management, and any weak sales can be blamed on the temporary pandemic slump in airport investment.
The training program costs little to maintain and supports the installed base of airport systems, and pandemic travel restrictions offer a temporary explanation for low uptake.
Airfield ground lighting training is closely tied to the firm's central AGL business and is cheap to sustain, so management would keep it despite lower demand during the pandemic.
The collaboration software fits the firm's announced digital airport strategy, so management would persist and attribute weak traction to airports' reduced spending during COVID.

The MLAT system was publicly announced at inter airport Europe as one of the most advanced products of its kind and represents a substantial surveillance investment, so escalation of commitment favors keeping it.
